text:
incident-bot: ALERT: cross-region routing anomaly (APAC -> US paths). Severity: P1. Trigger: latency-weight normalization error. Automated remediation attempted and failed.

liam: noticing p99 spike for apac1 -> us-east, lots of 502/503s from our edge proxies. Charts show weight collapse to single region for a subset of prefixes.

tara: confirmed from perf dashboards. The latency-weighting aggregation returned INF/NaN for a few buckets after the midnight retention sweep. That caused the normalizer to blow up.

owen: is this the same math bug we patched months ago?

nina: looks different. This is impacting pinning: some user IP ranges got pinned to a remote region because local weight went to 0. Customers seeing high tail latency and some request errors. Support reports ~1.2k active sessions affected, mostly realtime features (websocket upgrade failures).

pagerduty-bot: Paging platform-oncall: liam. Escalation sent.

liam: I'm oncall. Initial mitigation proposal: 1) switch traffic to stable-route-policy (non-latency-weighted) 2) apply emergency prefix pins for top 10 affected customers 3) bump DNS TTL to accelerate convergence for stuck clients. Any objections?

tara: go ahead with (1) and (2). DNS TTL bump is risky — we'll prefer application-level routing pins first.

liam: applying policy rollback now -> ```POST /api/v1/routing/set_policy {"policy":"stable-route-policy","reason":"incident 4977777777 rollback"}```

incident-bot: policy change queued -> complete in 18s.

liam: policy switched. Telemetry: traffic shifting off the bad region, p50 looks ok, p99 decreasing but still noisy.

owen: I'm pushing prefix pins for the top 10 customers: ```PUT /routing/pin {"prefix":"203.0.113.0/24","region":"apac1","duration":"1h"}``` repeating for list.

nina: support: draft update ready -> "We detected routing instability that temporarily shifted traffic away from nearest regions for some APAC customers. We've reverted to a stable routing policy and applied short-term pins to affected accounts. We're monitoring and will share a full update"

support-bot: customer-notice queued to support channel and affected accounts list attached.

liam: logs from policy-evaluator: ```ERROR policy_evaluator.py:normalize_weights() -> division by zero for bucket_count = 0; result = NaN```

tara: interestingly, the histogram purge job ran at 00:10 UTC and cleared low-volume buckets. The aggregator didn't guard for zero counts. We should also look for metric ingestion delays from apac-edge.

owen: quick fix idea: if histogram_sum == 0 then fallback to capacity_score or last_known_weights. That's a tiny change. But deploying policy code mid-incident is higher risk. We already reverted to stable policy; I'd prefer a targeted patch and canary next release.

liam: agree. For now, keep stable-route-policy and maintain pins until we validate patch in staging. Also increase sampling for APAC to avoid empty histograms.

incident-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF scheduled at 4977778200 from liam -> owen.

liam: handoff notes for owen: rollback applied, pins applied, support notified, root-cause likely histogram purge + aggregator guard missing, next steps: implement guard, add unit tests, schedule canary, review purge schedule and sampling.

own: taking over. I'll watch for any reappearance of NaNs and check if any clients still stuck on old routes. I'll coordinate with networking to check DNS caches (some clients use long-lived resolvers).

nina: customer impact numbers: 1,180 active sessions affected, 27 customers with >5% error increase. Most recovered after rollback. We'll send a follow-up with timeline and RCA.

liam: leaving doc comments: correlate purge job cron logs, check metrics ingestion for apac-edge proxies between 23:50-00:20 UTC, and add alert for histogram-empty condition.

own: I'll open the patch PR and link the canary once ready. ETA for PR: 3.5 hours. ETA for canary deploy: 6 hours.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 1: mitigation performed (policy rollback + pins). Monitoring continuing.

nina: thanks all. Support will keep the affected accounts updated. Closing communication loop with sales for high-touch customers.

owen: will keep monitoring p99 and websocket success rates for the next hour, escalate if anything looks bad.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring.

liam: good job team. We'll draft a postmortem after the patch and include lessons on purge scheduling and metric guards.
